target: AArch64 PCI QEMU, one vCPU, VirtIO keyboard and VirtIO sound WAV backend
command: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-current-retest.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody editor opens, recording is enabled, and H enters a C note
QEMU WAV capture contains C5 in four 50 ms windows
Shift+Escape exits playback, the graphical terminal evaluates 40+2 as 42, and zstatus reports failed=0
the experimental sound timer delivered nine IRQs
limits: Automated QEMU/WAV evidence only. Live UTM audible Psalmody playback is not confirmed by this run. The Pi user previously reported hearing a short note and Oh Great through HDMI, but the tested card's exact image provenance was not verified.
